newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn, SPD now headed for clash on pension reform.
newsitem.headline: Bonn, SPD now headed for clash on pension reform.

text.p: The German coalition and opposition Social Democrats (SPD), only days after coming to a deadlock on tax reform, on Saturday appeared headed for a clash on pension reform next week.

When the lower house of parliament meets on Tuesday, the coalition planned to propose a one-point increase in the value-added tax to 16 percent to finance lower paycheck deductions for the pension system, Wolfgang Schaeuble, a top lieutenant of Chancellor Helmut Kohl, said in an interview.
But a member of the SPD, which wants to raise the money by taxing fuel oil, said he saw no chance for a compromise with the coalition.
"We have already made so many compromises. That's it," Rudolf Dressler told the Welt am Sonntag in an interview due to appear on Sunday.
Schaeuble told the newsweekly Der Spiegel that the fuel tax hike alone was not enough to offset the pension cuts.
"The larger German states would be against raising gas taxes by the 15 or 20 pfennig that would be necessary" without additional financing, Schauble said.

The pension reform plan has already passed in the lower house but not the SPD-controlled upper house, where Social Democrats and Greens also want cuts in paycheck contributions for unemployment insurance. They want to finance these by raising fuel, gas and heating oil taxes as well as VAT.
